comparison: Perfect agreement on bone transplantation model characterization (C6-C43). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the model well-characterized with convincing evidence for injury and regeneration dynamics. Peer reviewers note the model is 'somewhat artificial' but accept the characterization data as valid.

Complete agreement on lineage tracing evidence (C44-C50). Both evaluations accept the high percentages and multiple genetic models as robust support for graft-derived BM-MSCs and dual endothelial origin. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Full agreement on functional recovery evidence (C51-C54). Both evaluations accept the qPCR and CFU-F data demonstrating functional equivalence. Peer reviewers previously requested additional confirmation but now accept the data as addressing their concerns.

Complete concordance on P-SSC expansion and migration (C55-C63). Both evaluations find the flow cytometry, microscopy, and periosteum removal experiments convincing. Peer reviewers' previous concerns about periosteal removal completeness have been addressed.

Agreement on P-SSC molecular characterization (C64-C70), though peer review also includes early transcriptional reprogramming claims (C71-C73) that OpenEval addresses separately in R6. Both accept the multi-level evidence for distinct P-SSC characteristics without challenge.

OpenEval separately evaluates early transcriptional reprogramming (C71-C73) as supported, while peer review groups these claims with broader P-SSC characterization (C64-C73). Both evaluations accept the RNA-seq and GSEA evidence without concerns.

Significant disagreement on intrinsic stress resistance (C74-C75, C13, C114-C115). OpenEval finds the ex vivo experiments provide strong evidence by eliminating environmental confounders. Peer Reviewer 3 expresses uncertainty, noting the metabolic stress condition was not well-justified and ex vivo purified cell studies may introduce artifacts.

Perfect agreement on periosteum wrapping experiment (C76-C81). Both evaluations find the evidence for P-SSC migration and functional reprogramming convincing. Peer reviewers' previous concerns about reporter allele confirmation have been addressed.

Agreement on Postn-CreER lineage tracing (C85-C87, C93), though peer review also includes transcriptional reprogramming claims (C90-C92) that OpenEval addresses separately in R11. Both accept the high percentage of Tomato+ BM-MSCs as strong evidence for periosteal origin.

Divergent evaluations of irradiation experiment (C88-C89). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the interpretation is speculative and alternative explanations are not tested. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the comparative finding without challenge to contextualize the transplantation model.

OpenEval separately evaluates transcriptional reprogramming evidence (C90-C92) as supported based on RNA-seq, PCA, and gene expression data. Peer review groups these claims with Postn-CreER lineage tracing (C85-C87) and accepts both without challenge.

OpenEval evaluates background/context claims (C1-C29) as supported by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically do not assess background literature claims.

Major disagreement on main conclusions (C107, C116-C117). OpenEval finds discussion claims well-supported by experimental data. Peer Reviewer 3 expresses uncertainty, arguing the authors do not definitively demonstrate that P-SSC migration is required for hematopoietic recovery, noting recovery occurs before significant migration and even after periosteum stripping.

OpenEval evaluates Postn marker rationale (C82-C84) as supported by citations and RNA-seq data. No corresponding separate peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers accept the use of Postn-CreER in their evaluation of R8.
